2608.07353.title: Geo-Spatial Concept Probing of Large Language Models: Abstraction, Compositionality, and Grounding
2608.07353.paper_summary: Understanding concepts is fundamental to generalization. Despite their impressive performance on a wide range of tasks, Large Language Models (LLMs) still struggle with genuine concept understanding. Prior work has evaluated conceptual understanding in LLMs using natural-language benchmarks or narrowly scoped synthetic tasks, but these settings often conflate multiple skills or lack precise control over the underlying concepts and their properties. To support controlled probing of concepts in LLMs, we design tests on their core properties: abstraction, compositionality, and groundness. We set up a concept-centric benchmark, targeting spatial concepts such as direction, distance, topology, and their compositions, and use question answering tasks serving as a proxy. We conduct extensive experiments across multiple LLM architectures and training regimes to analyze how model scale and design impact conceptual understanding. The results reveal clear limitations in current LLMs and provide insights into the factors shaping their ability to acquire and compose structured concepts. Our findings shed light on how concept-based LLMs can be redesigned for improved information access and knowledge management. The code will be available at https://github.com/rd20karim/concept-probing.
2608.07353.paper_summary_zh: 理解概念對於概括是基本的。儘管大型語言模型（LLMs）在各種任務上表現出色，但它們在真正的概念理解上仍然存在困難。先前的研究使用自然語言基準或狹窄範疇的合成任務來評估LLMs的概念理解，但這些設定往往混淆了多種技能，或缺乏對基礎概念及其屬性的精確控制。為了支持對LLMs中概念的控制探測，我們設計了針對其核心屬性的測試：抽象性、組合性和基礎性。我們建立了一個以概念為中心的基準，針對空間概念，如方向、距離、拓撲及其組合，並使用問題回答任務作為代理。我們在多個LLM架構和訓練模式中進行了廣泛的實驗，以分析模型規模和設計如何影響概念理解。結果揭示了當前LLMs的明顯限制，並提供了塑造它們獲取和組合結構化概念能力的因素的見解。我們的發現闡明了如何重新設計基於概念的LLMs，以改善信息訪問和知識管理。代碼將在 https://github.com/rd20karim/concept-probing 上提供。
